To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) breast cancer survivors who experience body image distress and low self-compassion are more likely to have a negative body image and (2) body image distress and self- compassion mediate the relationship between body image and distress.
breast cancer survivors with a negative body image and high distress have low self-compassion, while survivors with a positive body image and low distress have high self-compassion.
Breast cancer survivors who had a positive body image, low distress and high self-compassion had a more positive body image after treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how women with breast cancer experience their changed bodies, how they cope and what helps them to cope.
women's experiences of body image, distress, self-compassion and body change after breast cancer.
how women with breast cancer experience their body and body image, how they experience distress and how self-compassion can be helpful in the process of coping with a changed body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between body image and self-compassionate thoughts is not yet clear.
breast cancer patients are more likely to experience negative body image and body dissatisfaction, as compared with the general population and other cancer groups.
breast cancer survivors experience a changed body image and body image distress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that breast cancer survivors experience body image distress and this is related to self-compassion and self-compassionate behaviours.
we found a significant relationship between body image, distress, and self-compassions in women with a breast cancer diagnosis.
the body is an integral part of the cancer experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way you think about your body can affect your health.
the body image concerns of women with breast cancer are not limited to the breast.
the body image concerns of women diagnosed with breast cancer are not just about appearance, they are also about the body's ability to perform its functions.
